name: De Leonism
summary: De Leonism, the doctrine of Daniel De Leon and the Socialist Labor Party of America, holds that workers must organize in revolutionary industrial unions while also building a socialist party to win the ballot and declare the capitalist state dissolved. Power would then pass to an All-Industrial Congress of delegates chosen by industry and recallable at any time, which replaces territorial government and eventually leaves no political state. It rejects reformism, craft unionism and vanguard parties, and is held to be impossibilist, majoritarian and anti-Leninist.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: De Leon says the subdivision of labor aids cooperation and is necessary to the plentiful production that civilization requires, and that it compels a harmonious working together under a central directing authority. He treats it as something to keep under socialism, not abolish.

abolish-ip.rationale: De Leon argued that invention is social in scope and methods and that its nature demands the social ownership of its creations, not a lone inventor's property.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: De Leon made abolition of the wages system the single demand: ultimately wagism is to be abolished and the workers get the full product of their toil. Hass says the same.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: De Leon called international arbitration a humbug and nonsense in the mouths of the capitalist class meeting at the Hague.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: De Leon said the revolution needs the masses and excludes the idea of conspiracy, called the Paris Commune fruitless heroism, and said syndicalism has no place in the United States.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Hass says that under socialism machinery would cut hours rather than jobs, bringing a four-hour day. De Leon wrote that hours should fall in proportion to progress in invention once machinery is common property.

basic-income.rationale: De Leon wrote that socialism would ordain that all have equal opportunity to earn their living and that none shall live who do not work. That conflicts with an unconditional income.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: De Leon wrote that external peace cannot be stable where internal war is the social principle and that capitalists are at one another's throats internationally. Hass says modern wars result from economic competition in class-divided society.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: De Leon says competition first raised the pillars for the socialist republic and that the corporation began as a progressward combination bringing economy for waste. He says the capitalist at first filled a useful place as captain of industry but now only coerces, so capitalism's progress is past.

central-planning.rationale: De Leon said production under capitalism is left to anarchy and that socialism needs a central directing authority for production, as an orchestra needs a conductor. Hass describes an industrial government administering production nationally; neither source compares planned output with market output.

character-from-environment.rationale: Petersen's account of De Leon says that calling human nature unalterable begs the question and that men and women need not be reconstituted for socialism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: De Leon called charity an insult and a degradation and a weapon in the capitalists' hands, and said charity schemes are run by the capitalist class for its own ends. He did not offer government programmes as the alternative, so the answer is only that he rejected charity as the remedy.

class-collaboration.rationale: De Leon denied that capital and labour are brothers and condemned the AFL's theory of their common interest. Hass calls the idea of capital and labour as brothers fatuous.

class-struggle-history.rationale: De Leon wrote that economic classes take the place of the species in the struggle, that the law is struggle and not piping peace, and that class struggle is the basic principle. Petersen presents the materialist conception of history as the basis of De Leon's science.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Petersen describes the Industrial Union Government as non-political and classless, and De Leon described socialism as ending class rule.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Hass criticises the AFL and CIO for holding that the way to secure workers' well-being is signed contracts through collective bargaining, which he links to the false doctrine of brotherhood between capital and labour.

decide-locally.rationale: De Leon described a democratically centralised government accompanied by democratically requisite local self-rule, naming both the central and the local level without ranking them.

direct-action.rationale: De Leon rejected syndicalism and the sabotage and bombism preached in industrial unionism's name, and held that the union must unite the workers on the political field as well as the industrial.

direct-votes.rationale: De Leon described referendums and similar devices as the external tinkerings to which reform limits itself.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Socialist Standard's account says De Leon planned a labour-voucher system after the revolution, and criticises him for not providing free access. It does not report him envisaging distribution by need.

economic-freedom.rationale: De Leon wrote that equality before the law is possible only between men who are economically free. Hass says economic power is the source of political power.

four-day-week.rationale: Hass says automation and ending capitalist waste could bring the four-hour day and 16-hour week within a couple of years. De Leon expected hours to fall nearer three than eight a day.

gradual-change.rationale: De Leon called reforms mere patches, said the SLP would not take time from the main battle for revolution, and demanded unconditional surrender of capitalism rather than any first or temporary step.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: De Leon called the capitalist class a sponge that does no useful work, and objected that capitalism treats wealth as the reward of idleness and labour's product as the capitalist's.

industrial-unions.rationale: De Leon calls the Industrial Union both the battering ram against capitalism and the successor of the capitalist social structure, and he attacks craft or pure-and-simple unionism as having promoted workers' wretched conditions. He wanted the working class organised by industry, not by craft, in the Industrial Workers of the World.

informal-organisation.rationale: De Leon held that revolution needs open and above-board organising by an integrally organised union and wrote that without organisation there is no freedom.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: De Leon held that labour alone produces all wealth and that wages are the part of the product the capitalist hands back. Petersen's account describes value as the labour-power crystallised in goods.

land-value-tax.rationale: De Leon dismissed the Henry George single-tax movement as one of the charlatan booms resting on half-idiotic reasoning that disappointed the workers.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: De Leon says the paternalism of socialism ordains that all shall have equal opportunities to earn their living and that none shall live who do not work. He does not discuss a legal requirement or exemptions for those unable to work.

limit-guns.rationale: De Leon cited the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms as part of the individual's sovereign rights, and condemned troopers' warrantless house-to-house searches for weapons in a mining strike.

local-essentials-public.rationale: De Leon called public ownership of public utilities, and New Zealand-style government enterprises, abortive attempts to head off full class-conscious socialism, so he did not take local public ownership under capitalism as the remedy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: De Leon granted that competition served an early stage of production but called it wasteful and a driver of concentration, expecting social production and ownership to replace it. He did not say markets allocate better than collective control.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: De Leon held that morality follows the material plane, as slavery ended when machinery made it unprofitable and moral sentiment only aided revolution. Petersen presents the materialist conception of history as the basis of De Leon's social science.

material-over-identity.rationale: De Leon treated race riots as competition between wage slaves for jobs and not racial hatred. The Socialist Standard reports him charging Connolly with introducing racial and religious questions into the party.

means-match-ends.rationale: De Leon wrote that goals determine methods and that industrial unionism is the Socialist Republic in the making. He called the economic organisation the embryo of the future government.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: De Leon wrote that physical force lies in the structure of the economic organisation and not in military or other organisation implying violence.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Socialist Standard review says De Leon ousted James Connolly from the SLP, accusing him of introducing racial and religious questions into party tactics and organisation. It does not give De Leon's views on religious parties in wider politics.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: De Leon welcomed reform of divorce law and said marriage in the tribal era lasted as long as both parties consented and ended when consent ended. He mocked those who cry free love.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: De Leon called charity an insult and a degradation, and described the Carnegie and Rockefeller gifts as semi-restitutions of stolen social wealth, not a duty of the wealthy being fulfilled.

one-party-rule.rationale: Hass says the SLP, once elected, adjourns the political State and disbands, and Petersen condemns the Stalinist system of rule as the antithesis of Marxism.

organic-representation.rationale: De Leon proposed industrial constituencies to the total exclusion of political constituencies, with government made of representations from useful occupations. Hass says the SLP disbands after victory.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Hass describes a peaceful, legal revolution by the ballot, but De Leon called ballotism alone parliamentary idiocy and held that the union must supply the might to enforce the vote.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Hass has workers vote by shop unit and plant union, elect foremen and representatives, and hold complete democratic control of their tools and products. De Leon likewise wanted industry under the direct control of those employed in it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: De Leon said the revolutionist submits to the majority and that obedience is the badge of civilised man, and he demanded discipline in the party. Petersen's account stresses his strictness on this.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: De Leon wrote that under class rule women became chattels and vassals, held to a stricter moral standard than their husbands.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: De Leon wrote that the physical force of the revolution lies in the structure of the economic organisation, not in violence, and condemned preaching sabotage and murder. He still said the ballot should be backed by other means if the capitalist class rebels.

positive-liberty.rationale: De Leon wrote that equality before the law is possible only between men who are economically free, and that private property in the social tools breeds economic despotism and industrial slavery.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: De Leon says the capitalist papers are set up by moneybags for private profit and speak for Sir Moneybags, because the multitude has no wealth to set up such papers. He does not speak of press freedom as such.

production-for-use.rationale: Hass presents the industrial-union aim as production for the use of the producers and for the benefit of all, not for sale with a view to profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: De Leon held that the capitalist class does no useful work and lives on the labour of the workers: in his example a worker produces four dollars, is paid one, and the capitalist pockets the rest. Petersen's account gives the same surplus-value explanation.

property-fundamental.rationale: De Leon, citing Franklin, held that private property is a creature of society and subject to society's call, and that private property in the social tools breeds economic despotism and industrial slavery.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: De Leon rejected the theft, murder and sabotage preached in industrial unionism's name and condemned the pure and simple bombism of the AFL and the IWW.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In A Test Point De Leon argued, with Franklin, that private property is a creature of society and subject to its calls, and that society may change the system of ownership by experience of what makes people happy.

public-ownership.rationale: De Leon defined socialism as collective ownership and control of the necessaries of production by the whole people, and the SLP's Hass says industry must be owned socially and run democratically. He did not count nationalisation under capitalism as a step towards it, since wage slavery would remain.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Verso says De Leon argued at international congresses against immigration restrictions, and he condemned the craft-union resolutions on inferior and backward races.

recall-officials.rationale: Hass says the rank and file can recall and replace representatives and administrators whenever a majority of their industrial constituents so decide.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Hass says the rank and file elect administrators and representatives at all levels and can recall them whenever a majority so decide.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Verso says De Leon argued at international congresses against immigration restrictions, and he listed anti-immigration among the craft-union principles he condemned.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: De Leon said that for a class in thralldom revolution must become the moving spring, that the Constitution's amendment clause legalises revolution, and that revolution, peaceful or bloody, is a change from within.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: De Leon says socialism exposed the wife's status of pledging to obey her husband, lord and master, and welcomes placing husband and wife on an equality of duty. He does not discuss authority in marriage in so many words.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: De Leon called reforms mere patches and sought the overthrow of the political State and its substitution by the Industrial Social Order, so he did not ask that change respect established institutions.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Petersen's account says De Leon incessantly hammered home that a new government machine is needed to supplant the old State machine. De Leon wanted the political State overthrown and replaced by industrial government, and Hass says the SLP captures the political State to destroy it.

social-market-economy.rationale: De Leon called labour laws concessions wrung from capitalism and reforms mere patches, and sought to end the capitalist system itself. He did not favour a market economy with a safety net as the settled arrangement.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: Hass describes a peaceful and legal revolution through the ballot backed by an industrial union lockout, and De Leon located physical force in the structure of the union and not in military action.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: De Leon says the working class must unite on the political as well as the industrial field, since the revolutionary purpose can only be proclaimed on the political field. He also says a class not virile enough to strike a blow for itself is not fit for emancipation.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: De Leon cited the constitutional right of the people to keep and bear arms and condemned troopers' warrantless searches for weapons.

state-class-instrument.rationale: De Leon held that the State's functions turn from aiding production to oppression by property, and Hass calls the political State the executive committee of the capitalist class. Petersen's account likewise sees the State dying out with classes.

state-harmful.rationale: De Leon sought the overthrow of the political State, government apart from production, and its replacement by Industrial Government, while rejecting the anarchist slogan of no government. Hass says the SLP on winning adjourns the political State and disbands.

strong-leader.rationale: De Leon wrote that it is movements that make leaders and not leaders that make movements. Petersen contrasts De Leonism with Stalinism's blind obedience and distrust of the working class.

total-state.rationale: Hass says the industrial union movement does not want totalitarianism in any form, whether Stalinist, Nazi, Fascist or Franco.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Hass rejects totalitarianism whether Stalinist, Nazi or Fascist, and Petersen says Stalinism is hard to tell from Nazism.

traditional-family.rationale: De Leon wrote that under class rule the wife became a chattel and vassal, and welcomed divorce reform as a return towards marriage based on the consent of both parties.

unions-good.rationale: De Leon held that a class-conscious industrial union is indispensable ("no union, no Socialist Republic"). He attacked craft and pure-and-simple unions as props of capitalism, so the support is for industrial unions only.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Marx200 describes De Leonism as Marxist syndicalism in which the unions control the economy. De Leon called the industrial union the Socialist Republic in operation, and Hass has it administering production.

vanguard-party.rationale: De Leon said the Socialist organisation must be the head of the column of the proletariat, a minority so firm in principle that it carries the masses with it. Verso says De Leon held that only a political party with unity and clarity could lead the class.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: De Leon said the price of labour in the market has no floor but the pace of its decline and can be pared down to the wants of a beast, and he showed labour's share of product falling or stagnating at about a fifth. He did not state a fixed law returning pay to subsistence.

widespread-small-property.rationale: De Leon argued that efficiency demands large-scale production and that small manufacturers with inefficient machinery cannot hold out, looking to the wage-slave class to run large plants for itself rather than to small owners.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: De Leon said marriage should last only as long as both parties consent and should end when the consent ends, and welcomed placing husband and wife on equal terms.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: De Leon said that politics is not a private concern for a labour organisation and that the labour movement is essentially political.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: De Leon wrote that woman's degradation arose with class rule and that socialism foretold the restoration of her freedom as material conditions give plentiful wealth without arduous toil.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Verso quotes De Leon that the proletarian revolution must avoid, as it would a pestilence, all alliance with any other class.

worker-ownership.rationale: De Leon said socialism means turning the industries over to the direct control of the workmen employed in them, with collective ownership of the equipment of production. Hass likewise says the workers must own the industries socially and run them democratically.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Verso quotes De Leon that the proletarian revolution must avoid, as it would a pestilence, all alliance with any other class.

workers-councils.rationale: De Leon held that the central administrative organ of the Socialist Republic must be built of exclusively industrial constituencies in place of political ones, and Hass has an all-industrial union congress replacing the political Congress.

workers-nation.rationale: De Leon wrote that the working class of all nations has one enemy, the capitalist class of all nations, with its own nation's at the head of the list.

workers-own-party.rationale: De Leon held that the SLP alone was a genuine class party against the middle-class parties, and that the union should be a strict partisan of labour's politics. Hass presents the SLP as the workers' own political party.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: De Leon said the SLP, while not opposing reforms, sets its face against taking time from the fight for revolution, and held that immediate demands have no place in the platform.

workplace-democracy.rationale: De Leon wanted the industries under the direct control of the workmen employed in them. Hass has workers electing foremen and representatives at every level and able to recall them.

scope: De Leonism is the Marxism of Daniel De Leon and the Socialist Labor Party of America: socialist industrial unionism, a revolutionary strategy that joins a socialist party (the ballot) to revolutionary industrial unions and replaces the political state with an industrial government (s4, s5, s6, s10). It centres on De Leon's mature programme (c. 1890-1914), above all his Socialist Reconstruction of Society (the 1905 'Preamble to the IWW' address) and Two Pages from Roman History (1902) (s4, s5), and on the SLP's own later accounts of it by Arnold Petersen and Eric Hass (s8, s9, s10). It does not take in the later IWW, general syndicalism or Leninism, from which it is distinguished (s6, s13).

keyFigures.role: Founder and chief theorist of De Leonism, long-time leader of the Socialist Labor Party of America

evidence.quote: De Leon was also a co-founder of the Industrial Workers of the World and was active in the union until it split in 1908. In the wake of clashes with the IWW’s radical wing, De Leonism developed into an independent political current and to a Marxist form of syndicalism that strove for the control and management of a socialist economy through the trade unions.

De Leon’s major concern, states Coleman, was “to apply the orthodox position of Marx to the industrial conditions of his own time, and to simplify its reasoning and conclusions”. He goes so far as to include him in the tradition of popularising socialist ideas of William Morris and Robert Tressel and to write that it would be hard to name any other source of Marxian education in the USA. De Leonist bodies also emerged in Canada and Australia.

Previous installments in this series have focused on both the positive aspects of Daniel De Leon's political legacy, and the central political and economic incomprehensions of the De Leonist political tendency.
